audit_engine.scope: src/nav.js (navExport, navPlan, the gates, the ledger), src/data_nav.js (NAV_RULES, NAV_EU, NAV_FEES, NAV_MOSCOW), src/under.js (flowModel, arrAmount, premium via app.js SCHED), src/data_under.js (VENUES, DESTS, FX), src/data_atlas.js REGIMES, test.js block ‘v24: the Navigator’. Read-only; arithmetic re-run through a vm harness in the scratchpad (harness.js) that loads the live files.
audit_engine.note: The working copy changed under the audit: src/nav.js, src/data_nav.js and test.js were rewritten at 18:03 EST on 9 Nov 2026 while this file was being compiled, applying the preliminary findings (the diff credits ‘the auditor’). Each finding below carries a status field: ‘applied’ means the harness confirms the fix in the working copy at 18:03; ‘open’ means it still stands. Budget used: 15 searches, 25 fetches (one refused: sothebys.com is not on the allow-list; the schedule was read on the trade press instead).

findings.where: src/nav.js navPlan, the ledger (else-branch): line('impvat') and line('duty'); gate 4
findings.claim: Any route whose two ends differed charged the destination’s import VAT on the price, including routes between two EU members (fr→de showed ‘Import VAT in Germany (7.0%)’, $14,000 on a €200,000 painting; es→fr showed ‘Import VAT in France (5.5%)’), and the import gate was ‘conditional’.
findings.correct: A movement between two EU member states is not an import: no import VAT or duty at the border. The seller’s own VAT regime travels with the sale (none for a private seller; the margin scheme or the reduced rate for a dealer); only a VAT-registered buyer accounts for acquisition VAT at home. Import VAT is right only when one end is outside the EU customs territory.
findings.fix: Guard the impvat and duty lines with !intraEU and make the import gate ‘Within the Union: open’. Applied in the working copy (const intraEU; harness: fr→de import gate open, no impvat line; test ‘France to Germany’ added).

findings.where: src/data_nav.js NAV_RULES.in.exp.needs (and nav.js navHit)
findings.claim: India’s only row was {cat:'any', age:100, value:0, bar:true}; the declared art treasures sat in exp.artists but no row carried artists:true, so a 1935 Amrita Sher-Gil from India to London returned the export gate ‘Open — below the national thresholds (any work: 100 years)’.
findings.correct: Under the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act 1972 the works of the declared art treasures (Tagore, Sher-Gil, Jamini Roy, Ravi Varma, Nandalal Bose and others) may not be exported at any age, as the row’s own note said.
findings.fix: Add a row {cat:'any', artists:true, bar:true}. Applied (harness: Sher-Gil → ‘Closed: It may not leave: the declared art treasures…’; test added).

findings.where: src/data_nav.js NAV_RULES.kr.imp (was vat_rate 0.10, ‘10% VAT on import (U)’)
findings.claim: The Navigator charged 10% import VAT on a painting entering South Korea; the terminal’s own REGIMES row for Korea (src/data_atlas.js) says the opposite.
findings.correct: Korea exempts imports of 예술창작품 (original works of art) from VAT under VAT Act art. 27(15) with Enforcement Decree art. 56(17), because the basic customs rate on works of art is 0%; mechanically reproduced editions and printed reproductions are not ‘creative works’ and pay 10%, while hand-made original prints and photographs by the artist can qualify on the facts (2004 and 2019 rulings cited on the page).
findings.fix: vat_rate 0 for originals; vat_kinds for editions. Applied (vat_rate 0, vat_kinds {photo:0.1, paper:0.1}). Residual: ‘paper’ in the form means ‘a drawing or print’, and an original hand-made drawing is exempt; say in the note that the 10% is for editions and reproductions.
src: Taxly (Korean tax practice): 예술품 수입 면세, VAT Act art. 27(15), decree art. 56(17)

findings.where: src/data_nav.js NAV_RULES.*.imp.duty_rate (was 0 for all 22 jurisdictions) and nav.js ledger
findings.claim: duty_rate was 0 everywhere while the duty text said 5% (ae, qa, sa), 10% plus surcharge (in), ‘up to 6%’ (cn) and 4% (br); the ledger never showed a duty line and computed import VAT on the bare price.
findings.correct: Where a duty exists the ledger must carry it, and the import VAT/GST/IGST falls on the duty-paid value: UAE, Qatar, Saudi 5%; India 10% BCD plus the 10% social welfare surcharge on the duty (11% effective); Brazil 4% TEC; China 1% MFN (see the next finding).
findings.fix: Emit duty_rate from the research; VAT on price+duty. Applied for ae/qa/sa (0.05), br (0.04), in (0.11) and the VAT base (harness: UAE $800,000 sculpture → duty $40,000, VAT $42,000; India $500,000 → duty $55,000, IGST on $555,000). Still open for China (duty_rate 0).

findings.where: src/data_nav.js NAV_RULES.cn.imp (duty ‘reported at up to 6%… a cut to 1% could not be confirmed’; duty_rate 0) versus REGIMES.cn (‘1% duty… plus 13% import VAT’)
findings.claim: The two tables disagree on China’s duty, and the Navigator charges none.
findings.correct: China’s tariff for 9701.91.19 (other hand-painted oil paintings, pastels and other original paintings) shows an MFN rate of 1% (general rate 50%) and import VAT of 13%, per a tariff mirror (no tariff year stated; the MFN cut to 1% matches the REGIMES row). Retaliatory tariffs on US-origin art are a separate overlay.
findings.fix: Set NAV_RULES.cn.imp.duty_rate to 0.01 and rewrite imp.duty: ‘1% MFN duty on original paintings (9701.91) plus 13% import VAT on the duty-paid value’; keep the US-origin overlay in the text.
src: Treayo tariff mirror, China HS 9701.91.19: MFN 1%, VAT 13%

findings.where: src/data_nav.js NAV_RULES.in.imp.vat_rate 0.12 (‘IGST on import: 12% on paintings and sculpture (U)’) versus REGIMES.in (‘GST 5% on works of art since 22 Sep 2025’)
findings.claim: The Navigator charges 12% IGST on a painting entering India.
findings.correct: The 56th GST Council’s rate rationalisation cut chapter 97 (9701 paintings, 9702 prints, 9703 sculpture, 9705 collections, 9706 antiques) from 12% to 5% with effect from 22 September 2025; IGST on imports follows the GST rate, so the import charge is 5% on the duty-paid value (secondary source; notification number not seen).
findings.fix: Set NAV_RULES.in.imp.vat_rate to 0.05 and the text to ‘IGST 5% (from 12% on 22 Sep 2025) on value plus 11% duty’; the two tables then agree.
src: Disytax, HSN chapter 97 GST rates 2026 (12% → 5% from 22 Sep 2025)

findings.where: src/nav.js navPlan gate 4 and the ledger, from==='freeport' && navKey(to)==='ch'
findings.claim: A work leaving the Geneva freeport into Switzerland showed ‘The work does not cross a border’ and no VAT line, although the freeport gate said the 8.1% falls due on release.
findings.correct: Release from bond into Swiss free circulation is an import: 8.1% VAT on the value, no reduced rate for art.
findings.fix: Treat the release as an import. Applied (gate ‘Out of bond, into Switzerland: conditional’; ledger ‘Swiss VAT on release from bond (8.1%)’ $81,000 on $1m; test added).

findings.where: src/nav.js navPlan gate 1, the fundsRu branch (was ‘closed’ for every sanctioning sale-room country)
findings.claim: Money in a Russian bank closed the route with one text for all rooms: the CBR cap ‘on a resident’, Russian banks off SWIFT, ‘EU banks may not hold more than €100,000 (Article 5b)’, and the source-of-funds check — even for a New York sale to a US-resident buyer.
findings.correct: The grounds were banking practice and Russian capital controls, not a legal bar; the terminal’s own NAV_MOSCOW marks the same gates ‘conditional’ and says a New York sale to an unlisted buyer for US delivery is lawful under the EAR but commercially closed. Article 5b binds EU credit institutions only. The CBR cap applies to residents; non-working non-residents from ‘unfriendly’ states may not transfer abroad at all (CBR release).
findings.fix: Close only where a legal bar exists (buyer resident in Russia in a UK, EU or Swiss room; a shipment to Russia); otherwise ‘conditional’, law separated from practice. Applied (harness: New York, buyer US, funds RU → conditional; London, buyer and funds RU → closed; test added).
src: Bank of Russia press release, 23 Sep 2024: $1m a month to foreign accounts, $10,000 via transfer systems, ban for non-working non-residents from unfriendly states

findings.where: src/nav.js navPlan gate 1, the buyerRu branch for navKey(from)==='ch'
findings.claim: A Russia-resident buyer in a Swiss room was told ‘EU Regulation 833/2014, Article 3h, bars…’.
findings.correct: Regulation 833/2014 does not apply in Switzerland; the Swiss Ordinance on measures in connection with the situation in Ukraine (SR 946.231.176.72) mirrors the luxury-goods ban (CHF 300 per item in the data, flagged U).
findings.fix: Swiss branch in the ternary. Applied (harness: ‘the Swiss Ordinance on measures in connection with the situation in Ukraine mirrors the EU ban’). The CHF 300 figure and the SECO page remain unconfirmed.

findings.where: src/data_nav.js NAV_RULES.it.exp (rows bite on 70 years and €50,000 alone) and nav.js navExport
findings.claim: A 1949 painting by a living artist was told ‘A licence: paintings over 70 years old and €50,000’.
findings.correct: Art. 65(3)(a) D.Lgs. 42/2004 as amended by L. 40/2026 applies to works whose author is no longer living and whose execution dates back more than 70 years, above €50,000; a living author’s work needs only the self-declaration under art. 65(4)(b).
findings.fix: Skip the rows when the author is living. Applied (NAV_RULES.it.exp.dead=true and the filter in navExport; harness: Italy, living → open; test added). The form’s flag still conflates ‘living’ with ‘died within 70 years’, which matters only for the resale right.
src: Brocardi: D.Lgs. 42/2004 art. 65 as amended by L. 17 Mar 2026 n. 40 (€50,000; library goods €13,500)
Canella Camaiora: Law No. 40/2026, GU 30 Mar 2026, threshold raised from €13,500 to €50,000

findings.where: src/nav.js navPlan: const icg (was age>=200 && V>=€18,000 for any work entering the EU from outside)
findings.claim: The EU importer statement was required for any work over 200 years old and €18,000 entering the EU.
findings.correct: Regulation (EU) 2019/880 (applying since 28 June 2025) does not cover cultural goods created or discovered in the customs territory of the Union, so an 18th-century French painting returning from New York needs no statement; the licence (over 250 years, any value) is for archaeology and monument parts, the statement (over 200 years and over €18,000) for the rest.
findings.fix: A ‘made in’ field. Applied (navs.made: here/eu/noneu; harness: made in EU → no ICG sentence; made outside → ICG). The ‘here’ default treats a work in a non-EU country as made there, which is a guess the form should say.
src: Bundesamt für Kunstverwaltung (German federal art administration): EU Import Regulation 2019/880 — since 28 June 2025; licence over 250 years; statement over 200 years and €18,000; goods created or discovered in the EU excluded

findings.where: src/nav.js navPlan ledger, mode 'consign'
findings.claim: Sending one’s own work abroad to sell charged the destination’s import VAT on the value to the consignor ($50,000 on $1m consigned from New York to London).
findings.correct: A consignment to an auction house abroad enters under temporary admission: import VAT and duty are suspended; if the lot sells, the buyer pays the import VAT as an imported lot (5% on the hammer in London; 5.5% on hammer plus premium in Paris); the consignor pays nothing unless the unsold work is released into free circulation.
findings.fix: No impvat/duty lines for 'consign'; the gate names temporary admission. Applied (harness: us→uk consign → ‘Import at the border, under temporary admission: open’, no impvat; test added).

findings.where: src/nav.js NAV_SANCTIONING (had 'kr') versus NAV_RULES.kr.sanctions (‘art not covered’)
findings.claim: A route from South Korea to Russia was closed with the luxury-goods-ban text while the Korean row said Korea’s measures are export controls on strategic goods.
findings.correct: The data contradicted itself; the Korean row’s reading is the terminal’s own (U).
findings.fix: Remove 'kr'. Applied (harness: kr→ru → conditional).

findings.where: src/nav.js navPlan ledger, the model branch (flowModel was always called with imported:false)
findings.claim: An auction purchase in London or Paris was always a non-imported lot.
findings.correct: A lot under temporary admission carries 5% import VAT on the hammer in London and 5.5% on hammer plus premium in Paris for a buyer who keeps it in the country.
findings.fix: An ‘imported lot’ tick. Applied (navs.imported; harness: London→London imported $2.5m → VAT on premium $134,000, import VAT in the room $125,000 = 5% of the hammer).

findings.where: src/data_nav.js NAV_MOSCOW.gates[3] (‘Luxury-goods bans’): ‘it is prohibited to export works of art worth £250 or more to Russia or to make them available to a person connected with Russia’
findings.claim: The UK luxury-goods ban on works of art has a £250 threshold (sourced to a Women Art Dealers blog).
findings.correct: Schedule 3A of the Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, paragraph 21, reads ‘Works of art, collectors’ pieces and antiques, meaning any thing which falls within chapter 97’ with no sales-price condition, whereas neighbouring entries (sports articles, billiards and games consoles) carry ‘provided that the sales price per item exceeds £250’. The schedule was last amended on 20 May 2026 (S.I. 2026/543). NAV_RULES.uk.sanctions already says ‘no price threshold’, so the worked case contradicts the rule row.
findings.fix: In NAV_MOSCOW gate 4 replace ‘worth £250 or more’ with ‘of any value (Schedule 3A para 21 carries no price threshold)’ and add the legislation.gov.uk source; keep the ‘connected with Russia’ residence test.
src: legislation.gov.uk: Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, Schedule 3A (plain view), para 21 and paras 22–23

findings.where: src/nav.js navPlan gate 1 (fundsRu text: ‘the central bank caps a resident’s transfers abroad at $1m a month’) and NAV_MOSCOW.gates[0]
findings.claim: The CBR’s $1m-a-month cap is stated as a current rule without a date; the research dates its last confirmed extension to 1 Oct 2025–31 Mar 2026.
findings.correct: The limits ($1m a month to foreign accounts; $10,000 a month through transfer systems; a ban for non-working non-residents of unfriendly states) are confirmed on the Bank of Russia’s own release and were extended to 31 March 2026 (press of 26 Sep 2025). Whether they were renewed for April–September 2026 and beyond could not be checked within the budget; the Bank has renewed them every six months since 2022.
findings.fix: Date the cap in the gate text (‘last confirmed to 31 Mar 2026; renewed every six months since 2022’) and have the refresh script re-check cbr.ru each half-year.
src: Bank of Russia press release, 23 Sep 2024 (the limits)

findings.where: src/app.js SCHED (christies [[2e6,.28],[8e6,.22],[Infinity,.15]] ‘from 1 Sept 2026’; phillips 29/22/15 ‘from 12 Apr 2026’; bonhams five tiers ‘from 1 Oct 2026’) and data_market.js / data_houses.js fees
findings.claim: Christie’s and Sotheby’s share the 28/22/15 schedule; Phillips 29/22/15; Bonhams 30/28/25/21/14.
findings.correct: Sotheby’s is confirmed (below). For Christie’s the trade press confirms a change at the start of the September 2026 season but the report seen gives no figures; a May 2026 law-firm note had Christie’s at 27% to $1.5m, 22% to $8m, 15% above (since September 2025). Phillips 29% to $2m, 22% to $8m, 15% above is confirmed on the same note (effective date not given). Bonhams’ five tiers were not confirmed.
findings.fix: Flag christies and bonhams tiers S/U in the Lexicon until read on the houses’ own terms; the Navigator itself uses only the Sotheby’s schedule, so its ledger is unaffected.
src: Grossman LLP, Spring 2026 auction season: recent changes in buyer’s premiums, 14 May 2026
Antiques Trade Gazette topic page: ‘Christie’s and Bonhams amend buyer’s premium rates as new auction season begins’, 2 Sep 2026

findings.where: src/nav.js gate 7 and the usetax ledger line (‘Washington DC 6%’); DESTS/VENUES unaffected
findings.claim: The District of Columbia use tax is 6%.
findings.correct: 6% is the general sales and use tax rate through 30 September 2027; the rate rises to 7% for periods beginning 1 October 2027 (an increase delayed from 1 October 2025; secondary source, internally inconsistent on the year in its metadata).
findings.fix: Keep 6%; add ‘7% from 1 Oct 2027’ to the note and the refresh checklist.
src: Sales Tax Institute: DC general sales tax rate increases to 7% on 1 Oct 2027; 6% until then (posted 22 Sep 2026)

findings.where: src/nav.js navPlan ledger: const vat=(price+duty)*vatRate
findings.claim: Import VAT is charged on the price (plus duty) alone.
findings.correct: Import VAT is assessed on the customs value, which includes freight and insurance to the border (CIF) and, in Australia and Singapore, explicitly ‘value plus duty, freight and insurance’; the UK’s effective 5% is 20% on a quarter of that value. The omission understates the tax by the VAT on a few thousand dollars of freight, which is small at these values but not zero.
findings.fix: Add the freight and insurance lines’ midpoints to the VAT base, or say in the line’s note that the base is the price only.

findings.where: src/nav.js navExport (E.tax) and the exptax ledger line for routes from Spain to another EU member
findings.claim: Spain’s export tax is charged on a definitive export to any other country, including France (es→fr, 1880 painting, $1.5m → 30% band, $450,000).
findings.correct: The consolidated text of Ley 16/1985 art. 30 taxes ‘the export of any movable good of the Spanish Historical Heritage’ on the grant of the export authorisation, with three exemptions (goods lawfully imported within 10 years, authorised temporary exports, works by living authors) and no exemption for EU destinations, so the code follows the statute; whether the tax is in practice levied on movements to other member states (a charge of equivalent effect under EU law) was not established.
findings.fix: Keep the line; add to its note ‘on the statute’s wording, any destination; EU-bound movements unverified’ and have the research open the Ministry of Culture’s export page.
src: Normatia: Ley 16/1985 Título III, art. 30 consolidated (hecho imponible, exemptions, bands 5/10/20/30%)

findings.where: src/nav.js navPlan gate 2: obliged && V>=10000
findings.claim: The money-laundering gate turns ‘conditional’ at $10,000.
findings.correct: The UK and EU thresholds are €10,000 (single or linked transactions), about $11,200 at the model’s rate; a trivial gap, but the comparison should be in euros.
findings.fix: Compare V with 10000*FX.eur.

findings.where: src/data_nav.js NAV_RULES.fr.exp.needs ‘paper’ row (€20,000, prints) used for ‘A drawing or print’
findings.claim: A drawing from France is tested against the prints threshold (€20,000).
findings.correct: The 2021 thresholds are €30,000 for drawings, €50,000 for watercolours, gouaches and pastels, €20,000 for prints and posters; the row takes the lowest, which errs on the side of a licence.
findings.fix: Split the kind (drawing / watercolour / print) or say in the gate text that the lowest of the three thresholds is applied.
src: Ministère de la Culture, note d’information on Décret 2020-1718 (thresholds from 1 Jan 2021)

confirmed: Sotheby’s buyer’s premium from 13 Feb 2026: 28% to $2m / £1.5m, 22% to $8m / £6m, 15% above; wine and spirits 24% flat; the previous schedule was 27% to $1m / £800,000 (Antiques Trade Gazette, https://www.antiquestradegazette.com/news/2026/sotheby-s-raises-buyer-s-premium-to-28-at-the-lower-tier/; vf S). SCHED.sothebys and premium() match: $1m → $280,000; $2.5m → $670,000; $10m → $2,180,000 (harness).
Phillips 29% to $2m, 22% to $8m, 15% above (Grossman LLP, 14 May 2026; vf S); SCHED.phillips matches.

UK Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, Schedule 3A para 21: works of art, collectors’ pieces and antiques (chapter 97) with no sales-price threshold; paras 22–23 carry ‘exceeds £250’; last amended 20 May 2026 (legislation.gov.uk, https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2019/855/schedule/3A?view=plain; vf V). NAV_RULES.uk.sanctions is right.

UK export thresholds (ACE OGEL value limits): oil or tempera paintings £180,000; any other article £65,000; photographs £10,000; textiles £12,000; arms and armour £35,000; portraits of British historical personages £10,000; UK archaeology, manuscripts, archives and hand-made architectural/scientific/engineering drawings £0; all for objects over 50 years (https://www.artscouncil.org.uk/sites/default/files/download-file/UK%20OGEL%20Value%20limits.pdf; vf V). NAV_RULES.uk.exp.needs matches.

France, Décret 2020-1718 from 1 Jan 2021: paintings over 50 years €300,000 (was €150,000); watercolours, gouaches, pastels €50,000; drawings €30,000; prints €20,000; sculpture €100,000; photographs €25,000; other antiques over 50 years €100,000; printed maps over 100 years €25,000; the EU licence is now needed for exits to the UK (Ministère de la Culture note, https://www.culture.gouv.fr/Media/Medias-creation-rapide/Certificats-et-AST_modifs-decret-seuils_13-01-2021.pdf; vf V). NAV_RULES.fr.exp.needs matches.

Germany, KGSG § 24: third-country exports need a licence where Regulation 116/2009 applies; intra-EU thresholds category 3 paintings 75 years/€300,000; categories 4 and 7 (watercolours, sculpture) 75/€100,000; categories 5, 6, 8, 9 (drawings, prints, photographs, incunabula) 75/€50,000; category 12 archives 50/€50,000; category 14 means of transport 150/€100,000; category 15 other antiques 100/€100,000; other Annex I categories at the Annex ages and double the values; decision within 10 working days; a stay of up to two years exempt; works owned by their creator exempt (gesetze-im-internet.de, https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/kgsg/__24.html; vf V). NAV_RULES.de.exp.needs matches.

Italy, D.Lgs. 42/2004 art. 65(3)(a) as amended by L. 17 Mar 2026 n. 40 (GU 30 Mar 2026): works by deceased authors executed over 70 years ago need the attestato above €50,000 (was €13,500); library goods keep €13,500 (art. 65(3)(a-bis)); below the threshold a self-declaration under DPR 445/2000 whose validity equals the attestato’s (art. 65(4-ter)); loan authorisations within 90 days (Brocardi, https://www.brocardi.it/codice-dei-beni-culturali-e-del-paesaggio/parte-seconda/titolo-i/capo-v/sezione-i-bis/art65.html; Canella Camaiora, https://canellacamaiora.it/?p=37033; vf S). NAV_RULES.it.exp matches.

Spain, Ley 16/1985 art. 30: tax on the grant of the export authorisation; bands 5% up to 1,000,000 pesetas, 10% to 10,000,000, 20% to 100,000,000, 30% above, on the declared value as verified; exempt: goods lawfully imported within 10 years, authorised temporary exports, works by living authors (Normatia, https://normatia.com/es/normativa/patrimonio-historico-espanol/2026/titulo-iii-de-los-bienes-muebles/; Papelea, https://papelea.com/es/leyes/ley-del-patrimonio-historico-espanol/titulo-iii; vf S). The code’s euro bands €6,010 / €60,101 / €601,012 are the peseta limits at 166.386 (own arithmetic) and the band is applied to the whole value, as the statute reads; living artists skipped (!i.living) matches the exemption.

EU Regulation 2019/880: applies since 28 June 2025; import licence for archaeological objects and parts of monuments over 250 years old whatever the value; importer statement for other listed goods over 200 years old and worth over €18,000; goods created or discovered in the EU customs territory excluded (Bundesamt für Kunstverwaltung, https://www.kunstverwaltung.bund.de/EN/CulturalProperty/EuImportRegulation/EuImportRegulation_node.html; vf V). The icg test now matches (age, value and origin).

Apostille Convention (HCCH status table, 130 contracting parties, updated 30 Jun 2026, https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41+; vf V): United Arab Emirates and Qatar are not parties; Saudi Arabia in force 7 Dec 2022; China 7 Nov 2023; Singapore 16 Sep 2021; Canada 11 Jan 2024; Russia 31 May 1992; India 14 Jul 2005; Mexico 14 Aug 1995; Brazil 14 Aug 2016; Peru 30 Sep 2010; Japan 27 Jul 1970; Korea 14 Jul 2007; Switzerland 11 Mar 1973; Australia 16 Mar 1995. NAV_RULES.*.apost.hague matches for every jurisdiction in the terminal.

Korea: imports of original works of art (예술창작품) are VAT-exempt under VAT Act art. 27(15) and Enforcement Decree art. 56(17) because the basic duty on works of art is 0%; printed reproductions (basic duty 8%) and mechanically reproduced editions are not exempt (Taxly, https://taxly.kr/post/577-1-미술품은-면세-아닌가요-부가가치세--예술품-수입-면세-부수-면세; vf S). REGIMES.kr and the corrected NAV_RULES.kr agree.

China: 9701.91.19 (other hand-painted original paintings) MFN duty 1%, general 50%, import VAT 13% (Treayo tariff mirror, https://treayo.com/en/hs/china/97019119; vf S). REGIMES.cn (1% + 13%) is right; NAV_RULES.cn still needs the 1%.

India: GST on chapter 97 (9701, 9702, 9703, 9705, 9706) 5% from 22 Sep 2025, down from 12% (Disytax, https://disytax.com/hsn-97-works-of-art-gst-rate/; vf S). REGIMES.in is right; NAV_RULES.in.imp.vat_rate still says 12%.

Bank of Russia transfer limits: $1m (or equivalent) a month to accounts at foreign banks for residents and non-residents of friendly states; $10,000 a month through money-transfer systems; a ban for non-working non-residents of unfriendly states and for unfriendly-state companies (cbr.ru, https://www.cbr.ru/press/event/?id=21023; vf V); extended to 31 Mar 2026 (Snob and Profile.ru, 26 Sep 2025; vf S). NAV_MOSCOW gate 1 matches.
District of Columbia general sales and use tax 6% through 30 Sep 2027, 7% from 1 Oct 2027 (Sales Tax Institute, 22 Sep 2026; vf S). The Navigator’s 6% is right today.

Arithmetic of flowModel (harness, vf V): London home $1m hammer → premium $280,000, 20% VAT on the premium $56,000, resale right £9,393 → $12,405 (4/3/1/0.5/0.25% bands on £757,174, under the £12,500 cap), buyer $1,348,405; an imported London lot adds 5% of the hammer ($50,000); Paris home → 20% on the premium $56,000 and the resale right €9,735 → $10,890; a Paris imported lot → 5.5% on hammer plus premium ($70,400) in place of the premium’s VAT; Geneva home → 8.1% on hammer plus premium ($103,680), none into the freeport; New York home → 8.875% sales tax on hammer plus premium ($113,600); any room → Manhattan use tax 8.875% ($113,600) with no sales tax; London → Paris 5.5% ($70,400) and Paris → London 5% ($64,000) on the price; HK → Geneva 8.1% ($103,680). Export cancels the room’s VAT on the premium and an imported lot’s import VAT; the resale right survives export. The ledger’s lo/hi sums equal the sum of its lines (test).

Arithmetic of the Navigator (harness, vf V): London → Washington/New York, $2.5m at auction: premium $670,000; use tax $190,200 (DC 6%) to $281,338 (NYC 8.875%) on hammer plus premium; the UK licence bites at £180,000 (50 years); landed $3.37m–$3.48m, 8–26 weeks. Spain → London, 1880 painting $1.5m: 30% band → $450,000; 5% UK import VAT $75,000. UAE: 5% duty then 5% VAT on the duty-paid value ($40,000 and $42,000 on $800,000). India: 11% duty then IGST on $555,000. Freeport → Switzerland: 8.1% on $1m = $81,000. A loan carries a carnet and no use tax or import VAT; a consignment enters under temporary admission.

Logic confirmed (harness): the EU licence (Regulation 116/2009) is tested only when leaving the Union and never on a UK → EU route; Germany’s intra-EU thresholds and the EU thresholds are applied in the right order (de → us, 60-year €200,000 painting: no national licence, EU licence due); a bar closes the gate for a sale or a move and opens it for a loan (Kahlo, Sher-Gil, pre-1890 Brazil); Spain’s export tax is skipped for living artists and for loans; the freeport takes Swiss law (navKey → 'ch') and bond for the tax; the sanctions gate closes a shipment to Russia from every sanctioning jurisdiction whatever the buyer’s passport; a company owner only changes the screening text (the beneficial owner must be named).
unconfirmed: Christie’s 28% to $2m / 22% / 15% ‘from 1 Sept 2026’ and Bonhams’ five tiers ‘from 1 Oct 2026’ (the trade press confirms changes in September 2026, not the figures); the houses’ own pages were not reachable within the allow-list.
Whether the Bank of Russia renewed the $1m-a-month cap for April–September 2026 and October 2026–March 2027 (last confirmed to 31 Mar 2026).
Switzerland’s CHF 300 luxury-goods threshold and the SECO page; the Swiss AMLA CHF 100,000 cash rule (art. 8a) and the KGTG CHF 5,000 due-diligence line (carried from the terminal, not opened).

The GCC 5% duty on works of art for the UAE, Qatar and Saudi Arabia, Saudi’s 15% VAT, Brazil’s 4% II and 18% ICMS, Mexico’s 16% IVA and 0% duty, Australia’s 10% GST, Japan’s 10% consumption tax, Singapore’s 9% GST, Hong Kong’s zero (all plausible and consistent with memory; not re-opened this session).

The EU VAT rates the Navigator carries (France 5.5%, Germany 7%, Italy 5% since 1 Jul 2025 — the brief’s ‘Italy 10%’ is the pre-July-2025 rate —, Netherlands 9%, Spain 10%) and the UK’s effective 5% import VAT and 20% on the premium: carried from the terminal’s own primary citations (BOFiP, BMF, Assolombarda/Withers, Stb. 2025/339, Ley 37/1992, gov.uk), not re-opened.

The UK Artist’s Resale Right in sterling since 1 Apr 2024 (£1,000 threshold, £12,500 cap, bands at £50,000/£200,000/£350,000/£500,000) and France’s €750 threshold and €12,500 cap: the arithmetic matches Directive 2001/84 and the gov.uk guidance the terminal cites, but gov.uk was not opened this session.

US EAR Supplement No. 5 to Part 746 ($300 per unit for chapter 97) and EU Regulation 833/2014 Art. 3h (€300) and Art. 5b (€100,000): read by the research on a mirror and on K&L Gates / gesetze.legal; not re-opened.
New York’s non-resident purchase exemption (Tax Law §1118(2), TSB-A-08(7)S) and the credit for sales tax paid elsewhere; the DC credit rule.
Mexico’s list of artists declared artistic monuments (the data’s eleven names) and India’s nine declared art treasures beyond the five named in the row.
Whether Spain levies the export tax on definitive exits to other EU member states in practice (the statute’s text has no EU exemption).

The Phillips French and Geneva VAT guides behind VENUES.paris (5.5% on hammer plus premium for imported lots) and VENUES.geneva (8.1% on hammer plus premium): cited by the terminal with dates, not re-opened; Christie’s and Sotheby’s Geneva practice may differ (margin-scheme lots taxed on the premium only).
The ICG system’s name (EU CSW-CERTEX) and the 90-day licence decision period.
NAV_FEES (condition report, crate, freight, insurance 0.15–0.45%, broker, installation, legalisation): indicative trade figures from one shipper’s playbook; not re-checked.
